detailed_rationale:
Gujarat Ambuja Exports (GAEL) is a diversified agro-processor - corn/maize starch derivatives, soya derivatives, feed ingredients, edible oils and cotton yarn - serving food, pharma and animal-feed end markets, with likely exposure to India's ethanol-blending program via its maize/grain processing base (a structural, policy-driven volume tailwind), though I could not confirm an explicit ethanol-segment breakout from the sources available. Revenue growth has been consistently strong across the last four quarters (Sep-2025 +32.2% YoY, Dec-2025 +31.2%, Mar-2026 +15.8%, Jun-2026 +23.5%) - genuine, broad-based volume growth, not a single-quarter fluke, even though the 3-year revenue CAGR (~5.3%) is much lower, exactly the divergence our own growth_divergence_flag already caught.

Profitability, however, has been highly volatile - a classic agro-commodity input-output spread story. Operating margin swung from 10-11% (Sep/Dec-2024) down to just 4.9-7% (Mar-Sep 2025) before recovering sharply to 13% (Mar-2026) and 15% (Jun-2026), the highest level in the eight-quarter window. That margin collapse-and-recovery drove wild YoY profit swings (Sep-2025 profit fell ~45% YoY on the weak margin quarter, while Mar-2026 and Jun-2026 profit jumped +322% and +172% YoY respectively against the prior year's depressed base) - a real business improvement, not merely an easy comparison, since the absolute margin level achieved is also the best in two years.

Ownership is a clear strength: promoter holding is high and stable (63.84%, only gradually down from 66.18% in Mar-2017 - a decade-long, unremarkable drift), no pledge is disclosed, and leverage is low (D/E ~0.13x). At ~19.8-22x earnings, the valuation looks reasonable for a business that has just demonstrated its best margin quarter in two years, though the historical volatility argues for some caution about extrapolating the current 13-15% margin level indefinitely.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Sell on the 1-year lens (final_score_1y ~38.3), which I believe is anchored heavily on the trailing-twelve-month window that still includes the weak Mar/Sep-2025 margin-compression quarters, even though the growth_1y_score itself is high (78.2, correctly capturing the strong revenue trend). The two most recent quarters show a genuine, level-shift margin recovery (13-15%, the best in two years) on top of already-strong and consistent revenue growth, a high and stable promoter stake, low leverage, and a reasonable multiple - this is a rescue case, not a mismatch, so I am converting the score-Sell to Hold.
summary: Gujarat Ambuja Exports is a diversified agro-processing company (corn starch, edible oils, soya derivatives, feed ingredients) that has grown revenue strongly and consistently over the past year. Profitability had been volatile due to swings in input-output cost spreads, but the most recent two quarters show a genuine, meaningful margin recovery to the best levels in two years. Combined with high promoter ownership, low debt, and a reasonable valuation, we rate this a Hold.
positive_para: Revenue growth has been consistently strong (15-32% YoY) across the last four quarters - real, broad-based volume growth rather than a one-off - and the most recent two quarters show operating margin recovering to 13-15%, the best level in the eight-quarter window, translating into profit growth of 172-322% off a genuinely depressed prior-year base. Promoter holding is high and stable (63.84%) with essentially no leverage concern (D/E ~0.13x), and the ~20x multiple does not look demanding if the margin recovery holds.
negative_para: The margin history here is genuinely volatile - operating margin more than halved from 10-11% to under 5-7% within two quarters in 2025 before recovering, showing how exposed this agro-processing business is to input-output spread swings (maize/corn costs versus starch, edible oil and feed-ingredient realizations) that are largely outside management's control. The 3-year revenue CAGR of only ~5.3% versus the last year's 15-32% growth is a meaningful divergence, and until a few more quarters confirm the 13-15% margin level is sustainable rather than a cyclical peak, there is real risk of reverting toward the weaker 2025 margin experience.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~19.8-22x earnings, the valuation is reasonable if the recently-achieved 13-15% operating margin proves durable, given consistently strong revenue growth; it would look considerably richer if margins revert toward the 5-7% levels seen as recently as mid-2025, given how volatile the spread economics have shown themselves to be. Growth is below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies.
